papers.summary: Introduces spectral weight decay as a decoupled nuclear-norm update that shrinks smaller singular values more strongly. It reports lower effective rank, improved SVD-LLM compression and inference speed at matched validation loss, and improved robustness to label noise.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, effective rank, low-rank compressibility, and memorization under label noise.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 M to 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
At 500 M and a 4% distortion budget, it reaches 1.89× compression and a 1.18× GPU inference speedup.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Introduces Learnable Subspace Projections, which jointly learn discarded subspaces while keeping pretrained weights frozen. The reported Llama-2-7B experiments compare against several low-rank baselines under matched calibration and show substantial memory and decoding benefits, with limitations around local rank allocation and compression overhead.
papers.relevance: Strong match for learned low-rank compression, model-quality versus efficiency tradeoffs, and practical inference measurements.

evidence.quote: All baselines are using the same calibration budget of 1024 sequences of 2048 tokens.
At weights and FLOPs matched to within 2%, LSP decodes fastest at every ratio.

papers.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

papers.summary: Proposes sMuon, an efficient approximation of the Muon objective for low-rank adapters using linearization and least squares with matmul-only implementation. It reports favorable results across supervised fine-tuning and a ReLoRA pretraining experiment.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization for LoRA, low-rank parameterizations, Muon, and ReLoRA pretraining.

evidence.quote: Our method, sMuon (small Muon), performs favourably across SFT and a ReLoRA pretraining experiment.

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

papers.summary: Introduces Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation, which normalizes LoRA down-projection matrices during training or only at initialization. The method is reported to improve convergence, stability, performance, and catastrophic-forgetting behavior across pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning without extra trainable parameters or inference computation.
papers.relevance: Direct match for LoRA optimization dynamics, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, convergence, and stability.

evidence.quote: We introduce Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation (NoRA), a simple yet effective method that normalizes the down-projection matrices during training.
Across pretraining, supervised finetuning, and reinforcement learning, NoRA consistently accelerates convergence, improves performance and training stability, and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Proposes NorMuon, combining Muon’s orthogonalization with neuron-wise adaptive normalization. It analyzes non-uniform neuron norms and describes a distributed FSDP2 implementation for scalable deployment.
papers.relevance: Relevant to Muon optimization geometry, optimizer scalability, distributed training, and efficiency at LLM scale.

evidence.quote: NorMuon addresses this imbalance by maintaining second-order momentum statistics for each neuron and applying row-wise normalization after orthogonalization.
We develop an efficient distributed implementation under the FSDP2 framework.

papers.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable

papers.summary: Introduces Hybrid Momentum, combining linearly weighted historical gradients with geometrically discounted momentum, and HyMUON, which applies Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Controlled experiments span image classification, machine translation, and language modeling.
papers.relevance: Directly matches interests in momentum methods, Newton-Schulz approximations, and optimizer design.

evidence.quote: In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction.
Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales.

papers.title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models

papers.summary: Studies how optimizer rankings change with batch size. It argues that no principled Muon scaling rule works consistently across settings and explains the effect through direction-dependent curvature, gradient noise, and preconditioning bias-variance tradeoffs.
papers.relevance: Highly relevant to optimizer evaluation, scaling behavior, gradient noise, and training-efficiency tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: The best optimizer for language model pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning.
Gradient noise drives a bias-variance tradeoff in preconditioning that can reverse optimizer rankings across batch sizes.

papers.title: The Best Optimizer Depends on Batch Size

papers.summary: Presents AQL-Lite, a data-curation and partial-parameter continual-pretraining recipe using RS-LoRA together with selected transformer blocks and embeddings. The abstract reports gains over raw-data and adapter-only baselines while reducing training time relative to full-parameter continual pretraining.
papers.relevance: Relevant to memory-efficient LLM pretraining, RS-LoRA, partial updates, and quality-throughput tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: AQL-Lite couples a quality-first curation pipeline with a partial-parameter CPT recipe that trains RS-LoRA adapters across the network together with the last eight transformer blocks and the embedding matrix.
CPT on AQL-curated data raises a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over CPT on raw web text.

papers.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining

papers.summary: Introduces Signals and Queries, an embedding-based first-stage relevance filter for LLM agents. It uses offline-generated activating examples and hard negatives with independent logistic classifiers to reduce downstream evaluation while preserving recall and improving precision over top-K and cosine-threshold retrieval.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to paper retrieval, relevance ranking, context filtering, and application-controlled agent orchestration.

evidence.quote: A lightweight first-stage relevance filter developed for Parlant 4.0 that removes at least 30% of candidate policies before downstream evaluation while preserving high recall.
S&Q achieves higher precision than top-K and cosine-threshold retrieval at every evaluated recall level.

papers.title: Signals and Queries: Token-Efficient Agentic Context Discovery

papers.summary: Studies whether self-evolving LLM agents are continual learners when they modify prompts, memory, and skills while keeping model weights frozen. It evaluates retrieval and self-modification methods across drifting task streams and reports a stability-plasticity tradeoff caused by global edits.
papers.relevance: Strong match for building a research-digest agent with explicit context management, memory, retrieval, and a handwritten harness.

evidence.quote: They adapt by rewriting their own harness, such as prompts, memory, and skills, from task feedback while the model weights stay frozen.
Higher plasticity consistently comes at the cost of stability.

papers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
